misconceptions.description: Believing a flat ban on AI tools guarantees academic integrity in design work
misconceptions.trigger: policy states only that AI is prohibited and treats any use as dishonesty
misconceptions.feedback: A ban drives concealment and cannot distinguish generated work from bounded support; permit bounded use with disclosure.

misconceptions.description: Requiring AI disclosure without giving a concrete format students can follow
misconceptions.trigger: policy asks for disclosure but provides no example line or fields
misconceptions.feedback: Show one worked disclosure line (tool, prompt intent, accepted or rejected) so disclosure does not add invention load.

misconceptions.description: Writing a blanket AI clause that does not distinguish assistive tools from generative design work
misconceptions.trigger: policy sweeps screen-reader or alt-text AI into the same prohibition as generating an artifact
misconceptions.feedback: Name what the policy protects (the learner's design judgment) so assistive uses are not accidentally banned.
